A basic start/stop uses a seal-in (latch): pressing Start turns the output on, and the output then holds itself on until Stop or a fault breaks the circuit.

Stop buttons are normally wired as normally closed, so a broken wire also stops the motor.

lessons.c:
An interlock blocks unsafe or conflicting actions. Forward and reverse must never be on together, and a press may only run when its guard is closed. Interlocks are conditions ANDed into outputs.

Remember: program interlocks do not replace safety hardware. Emergency stops use safety-rated devices.
lessons.x: A reversing conveyor cannot start forward while the reverse output is on.
lessons.ex: List two interlocks for a machine with a sliding guard door.
